The Stuttgart-based collector has gathered dozens of historical turret clocks from across Germany and displays them in a former air-raid shelter. This coming Sunday, March 26, 2006, at 2:00 a.m., the time will be set forward by one hour, marking the start of daylight saving time. (AP Photo/Thomas Kienzle)

articles.title: Talarico cheers on Matthew McConaughey: ‘I think he’d be a great candidate’
articles.summary: Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico backed actor Matthew McConaughey getting involved in electoral politics. “If Matthew McConaughey feels strongly about it, he should step up and run,” Talarico told TMZ DC in a clip posted to the social platform X on Wednesday. “I think he’d be a great candidate,” the Texas Democrat added. Talarico’s…
articles.body:
Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico backed actor Matthew McConaughey getting involved in electoral politics.

“If Matthew McConaughey feels strongly about it, he should step up and run,” Talarico told TMZ DC in a clip posted to the social platform X on Wednesday.

“I think he’d be a great candidate,” the Texas Democrat added .

Talarico’s comments follow McConaughey sharing a message before the midterms, claiming that casting a ballot for independent candidates could bring lawmakers “back to the middle, where most American values live.”

In a video posted to X over the weekend, McConaughey said, “This is about the upcoming ballot, and I am not here today to endorse a candidate or a party.”

“I am here endorsing two things: fairness and reality,” the actor added. “I believe in a fair fight, and a fair fight is not just two fighters throwing the same punches at each other for 50 years. A fair fight is when the fighters who ought to be represented in the fight are actually in the fight.”

“The No. 1 political identity in America today is not Republican. It is not Democrat. It is independent,” McConaughey said.

According to a Gallup poll from 2025, 45 percent of American adults identified as independents, with 27 percent identifying as Republicans and another 27 percent identifying as Democrats.

“So independents belong in the fight — not as a protest, not as a spoiler — but as a real and potential winner, on the ballot and considered seriously by us,” McConaughey said.

When asked by TMZ why he is making his bid for the Senate “as a Democrat,” Talarico responded that, “because of this two-party system, it’s near impossible to be able to get elected as an independent candidate.”

articles.title: Thanksgiving weather outlooks released: What could it be like near you?
articles.summary: We’re about a month away from Thanksgiving week, and the weather outlooks are already available.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – Thanksgiving is more than a month away, but you may already be booking your flights – if you didn’t when experts recommended it last month – and planning your route (over the river and through the woods) to grandmother’s house.

If you’re worried about weather impacting your travel, you may be in luck, at least according to one outlook.

The Farmers’ Almanac says its forecast suggests there will not be “a major nationwide storm” during the week of Thanksgiving this year, specifically from Monday, Nov. 23 through Thanksgiving Day.

The publication is anticipating cooler temperatures for most of the U.S., with the exception of the Southeast, where it could be “mild and pleasant.” Snow is possible throughout the northern Plains and Rockies, as well as in the Midwest and Northeast. Rain could impact the Pacific Northwest and the Southwest, with “no major storminess” expected in the Southern Plains.

The Old Farmer’s Almanac, meanwhile, has a slightly different outlook for Thanksgiving.

Temperatures will trend warmer across most of the West and along the East Coast, and mild through New England and along the coast of the Pacific Northwest. For those in the Central U.S., from Minnesota and Wisconsin south to the Gulf, the almanac predicts temperatures will trend cooler.

There are snow chances in the northern Midwest and the possibility of rain in the Northwest, New England, Texas, and the Southeast.

There’s no major storm on the Old Farmer’s Almanac’s outlook, either.

It is, of course, difficult to say what exactly the weather will be like roughly a month from today. The Farmers’ Almanac even encourages readers to check in with the National Weather Service and the NOAA Weather Prediction Center closer to the holiday.

While the National Weather Service offers long-range weather outlooks, it doesn’t predict specific events, like a major storm while people are traveling for Thanksgiving, this far in advance because it’s not possible .

NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center did, however, release its early winter weather outlook last week. It also unveiled its 30-day forecast, covering parts of November.

Broadly speaking, the outlooks, seen in the slideshow below, suggest nearly everyone has a higher probability of seeing above-average warmth in November. The southern half of the country, meanwhile, has a higher likelihood of experiencing above-average precipitation.

Hawaii, while not pictured above, has a higher chance of above-normal temperatures from November through January and below-normal precipitation, according to the CPC .

These forecasts, which show the broad weather patterns we could experience, fall roughly in line with what is expected from the “historic” El Niño we’re facing .

NOAA and the almanacs review some of the same factors, including data on the El Niño. Whether or not you trust the almanacs’ outlooks, however, is up to you.

“While no forecast can claim perfect accuracy, our predictions have proven useful for generations of planners and outdoor enthusiasts,” Sandi Duncan, the editor of the Farmers’ Almanac, told Nexstar last year. “We continuously refine our method but acknowledge that Mother Nature always has the final say.”

images.caption: Snow falls on Thanksgiving Day, in Meredith, N.H., Thursday, Nov. 28, 2024. (AP Photo/Nick Perry)

articles.title: Supreme Court won’t revive Trump administration’s transgender inmate policy; Thomas, Alito dissent
articles.summary: The Supreme Court refused the Trump administration’s bid to stop providing transgender inmates hormone treatments and certain surgeries on Wednesday, declining to lift a lower judge’s block over the dissents of two conservative justices. The Bureau of Prisons (BOP) policy would taper treatments for inmates currently receiving them, and officials would also need to stop providing…
articles.body:
The Supreme Court refused the Trump administration’s bid to stop providing transgender inmates hormone treatments and certain surgeries on Wednesday , declining to lift a lower judge’s block over the dissents of two conservative justices.

The Bureau of Prisons (BOP) policy would taper treatments for inmates currently receiving them, and officials would also need to stop providing social accommodations, like hair-removal devices.

Solicitor General D. John Sauer asserted the changes are needed to maintain “institutional security” in federal prisons.

It’s a rare loss for the Trump administration, which has emerged victorious more than two dozen times in asking the high court for emergency relief after a judge blocked an aspect of the president’s agenda.

Justices Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, both members of the court’s 6-3 conservative majority, publicly dissented. Neither they nor the majority explained their reasoning.

Last year, the justices allowed the administration to enforce its ban on openly transgender troops serving in the military.

But now, the administration faces a Supreme Court loss in its fight against what it calls “gender ideology.”

The battle dates back to Trump’s first day of his second White House term. The president signed an order directing that no federal funds be spent on medical procedures “for the purpose of conforming an inmate’s appearance to that of the opposite sex.”

Affected prisoners, represented by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), have been suing for months. Their case now focuses on a February statement the BOP issued formalizing the restrictions.

“This is a critical ruling for our clients and all transgender people in Bureau of Prisons custody,” Li Nowlin-Sohl, senior staff attorney with the ACLU’s LGBTQ & HIV Project, said in a statement.

“The denial of medically necessary health care, including gender-affirming health care, to people in prison is a violation of their fundamental constitutional rights,” Nowlin-Sohl continued. “We will continue to defend the rights of our clients and all incarcerated people.”

The Trump administration said their lawsuit should fail for multiple reasons, including that the lower courts aren’t complying with a law that limits inmates’ ability to file endless civil litigation.

In court filings, the administration called it an “egregious intrusion into federal prison administration.” The administration brought the case to the Supreme Court after the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit voted 2-1 that there was no trace of any specific security incident under the old policy.

The ACLU says enacting the restrictions would upend that three-decades-long status quo.

“That glaring omission, as well as the unreasonableness of its decision, make it clear that the rationales were contrived to support the demand President Trump made in the EO,” the ACLU wrote to the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Ossoff leads Collins while Jackson, Bottoms nearly tied in Georgia: Poll
articles.summary: A new poll found Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) leading his GOP opponent Rep. Mike Collins (Ga.) in his reelection battle, while Republican Rick Jackson narrowly leads Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms in the Peach State’s gubernatorial race. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution and University of Georgia poll reported 48 percent of respondents supported Ossoff’s reelection bid, 40 percent…
articles.body:
A new poll found Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) leading his GOP opponent Rep. Mike Collins (Ga.) in his reelection battle, while Republican Rick Jackson narrowly leads Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms in the Peach State’s gubernatorial race.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution and University of Georgia poll reported 48 percent of respondents supported Ossoff’s reelection bid, 40 percent backed Collins and 12 percent were undecided.

The Journal-Constitution noted Ossoff led among women, young people and Black voters, though Collins held leads among people 65 and older and white voters.

Ossoff, the only Senate Democrat running for reelection in a state President Trump won in 2024, is running for his second term following a high-profile 2020 runoff election. He faced off against Collins earlier this month in a debate where the two clashed on the Jeffrey Epstein files, Trump’s tariffs and the war in Iran.

Collins alleged during the debate certain ads for Ossoff were paid for by a tech billionaire with ties to the convicted sex offender and disgraced financier. The billionaire in question, Reid Hoffman, said last year he was “never a client of Epstein’s and never had any engagement with him other than fundraising for MIT,” referring to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

Ossoff went on the offensive and referenced Collins’s votes against the release of the Epstein files in the summer of 2025 .

“Mike, who on your team advised you to raise the Epstein files? You voted to cover up the evidence,” the senator said. “You should explain that vote to Jeffrey Epstein’s victims right now.”

In the gubernatorial race, 46 percent of poll respondents backed Jackson, 45 percent supported Bottoms and 8 percent remained undecided. Jackson’s lead is within the poll’s margin of error, meaning the candidates are essentially deadlocked.

Bottoms led among independents at 43 percent, while 38 percent were supportive of Jackson and 18 percent of independent respondents were undecided.

The gubernatorial candidates are racing to fill the seat that will be vacated by retiring GOP Gov. Brian Kemp (R) as the contest remains one of the most closely watched races of the 2026 midterm election.

Ahead of Election Day, more than 188,000 Georgians cast their ballots on the first day of early voting, which is about 50,000 more than the number of people who voted early on Day 1 in 2022, according to the Georgia secretary of state’s office.

VoteHub credits the high early turnout to Black voters, who comprise more than 36 percent of votes cast as of Tuesday.

The Journal-Constitution and University of Georgia poll was conducted Oct. 7-15 among 1,000 likely Georgia voters. The margin of error was 3.1 percentage points.

articles.title: Pritzker’s wife donates $500K to Acton after Ramaswamy ad
articles.summary: Illinois first lady MK Pritzker announced Wednesday that she donated $500,000 to Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton’s (D) campaign after Republican Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign released a video featuring Acton’s estranged mother calling her daughter a “liar.” “Bad men gain power when we refuse to stand up and fight. Vivek Ramaswamy represents everything that is wrong…
articles.body:
Illinois first lady MK Pritzker announced Wednesday that she donated $500,000 to Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton’s (D) campaign after Republican Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign released a video featuring Acton’s estranged mother calling her daughter a “liar.”

“Bad men gain power when we refuse to stand up and fight. Vivek Ramaswamy represents everything that is wrong with our politics today: arrogance, cruelty, dishonesty, and the belief that it’s acceptable to say and do anything for power,” Pritzker, the wife of Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker (D), a possible 2028 presidential contender, said in a statement.

“This race is about standing up to bullies, confronting extremism, and making damn sure that men who thrive on cruelty and division don’t get a free pass to govern,” she added. “Ohio deserves better, Ohio deserves Amy Acton as their Governor, and I’m willing to fight for her.”

A video of Acton’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur, roiled the Ohio gubernatorial race on Tuesday when the one-minute spot circulated over social media. In the video, Arthur says her daughter has “a serious problem” and that she “lies about her past,” including growing up in a tent.

The video ends with Arthur urging Ohioans not to vote for Acton, saying “if you think she’ll make your life better, you’re fooling yourself,” though Arthur does not mention Ramaswamy by name.

Acton told The Vindicator during an August 2019 interview she was estranged from her mother. Acton’s stepfather Cledith Arthur abused her when she was an adolescent and was later charged with raping Acton, according to The Associated Press , which obtained court and police documents. Despite pleading not guilty to the crime, he was later indicted by a grand jury, according to the news outlet.

Acton’s brother Philip Stearns said in a statement responding to the video on Tuesday that their mother and stepfather lost custody of the children, adding that their mother remained married to her stepfather until he died.

Ramaswamy’s campaign said it produced the ad but Donna Arthur had not been paid for it. It was initially unclear who had released the video. Despite backlash over the ad from both Democrats and Republicans, the Ramaswamy campaign said they would be spending $4 million to promote it ahead of next month’s race.

“We don’t know what happened between Amy and her mother, who first spoke out about Amy in 2020, but we know that Amy Acton is a serial fabulist who has some serious problems with the truth that the public needs to be aware of before deciding who to entrust as governor,” Ramaswamy campaign spokesperson Connie Luck said in a statement regarding the ad.

Acton’s campaign slammed the ad, with Stearns saying “it’s not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at twelve years old from our birth mother’s husband into a political talking point.”

“This desperate, disgusting attack reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core – a pathetic excuse for a man who is willing to hurt anyone as long as it gets him what he wants,” he added.

Acton’s campaign also came out with an ad in response, in which Stearns says in a direct-to-camera video that the Ohio GOP rival is “ not fit to lead .” Acton’s brother also recounted their stepfather’s abuse.

Her campaign doubled down on those points in a new statement Wednesday in response to reporting that Ramaswamy’s team would be spending millions to promote the controversial ad.

“Vivek Ramaswamy investing $4 million to run a repulsive advertisement that gives star billing to Dr. Acton’s abusive mother is both despicable and entirely predictable from a scam artist who has spent this campaign standing alongside abusers and sex predators,” Acton campaign spokesperson Addie Bullock said in a statement.

The nonpartisan election handicapper Cook Political Report rates the Ohio governor’s race as a “toss-up.”

articles.title: Neil Bush, brother of George W. Bush, says he voted for Talarico
articles.summary: Former President George W. Bush’s brother announced Tuesday that he voted for Democrat James Talarico in the high-stakes Texas Senate race. In a post on Facebook, Neil Bush wrote that while he normally stays out of politics, he had serious concerns about Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the Republican nominee in the race. “I have…
articles.body:
Former President George W. Bush’s brother announced Tuesday that he voted for Democrat James Talarico in the high-stakes Texas Senate race.

In a post on Facebook , Neil Bush wrote that while he normally stays out of politics, he had serious concerns about Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the Republican nominee in the race.

“I have been deeply troubled by Paxton’s conduct as Texas Attorney General, particularly his decision to challenge the results of the 2020 presidential election,” Bush wrote. “My concerns about his judgment and conduct are hardly mine alone. He was impeached by the Republican-controlled Texas House, although subsequently acquitted by the Texas Senate.”

A spokesperson for the Paxton campaign did not immediately respond to The Hill’s request for comment.

Bush said his vote was not only to oppose Paxton. The former president’s brother praised Talarico’s character, saying he sees qualities in the Texas state representative that he admires in public servants.

“He speaks with respect, seeks common ground, and seems genuinely interested in bringing people together rather than driving them apart,” Bush wrote. “His faith appears to be a deeply rooted source of humility, compassion, and conviction rather than a political weapon.”

A Presbyterian seminarian, Talarico talks openly about his Christian faith on the campaign trail.

President Trump’s takeover of the Republican Party has put the GOP at odds with the Bush family.

The former president did not endorse Trump in 2024, and his daughter, Barbara Bush, endorsed and campaigned for former Vice President Kamala Harris. Former Vice President Dick Cheney, who served with Bush, endorsed Harris , along with his daughter , former Rep. Liz Cheney (R-Wyo.).

Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas), whom Paxton defeated in this year’s primary, held a fundraiser with the former president to support a handful of GOP Senate nominees in competitive races, but not Paxton.

And in 2022, former Texas Land Commissioner George P. Bush, the former president’s nephew, launched a primary challenge against Paxton for attorney general but lost in the runoff by a 36-point margin.

In Tuesday’s Facebook post, Neil Bush wrote that he still believes in Republican principles but believes Trump has done “enormous damage to the Republican party.”

“I have been a Republican for most of my life, and I still believe deeply in many traditional Republican principles,” Bush wrote. “But character matters more than party affiliation.”

articles.body:
Federal agents are investigating reports of an incendiary device being thrown at Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) downtown Atlanta office Tuesday night.

“FBI personnel and evidence response technicians are on site collecting evidence,” the FBI said in a statement obtained by NewsNation, The Hill’s broadcasting partner.

“There is no known threat to public safety at this time,” the FBI continued.

According to Atlanta news station WSB-TV, the FBI and Department of Homeland Security investigators were called to 180 Ted Turner Drive around 9:30 p.m. after city police initially responded to reports surrounding the device.

The station reported law enforcement collected evidence from a sidewalk near the building. It included a plastic lighter and a shopping bag, along with what appeared to be two bottles of lighter fluid.

ICE has faced mounting scrutiny over highly publicized use-of-force incidents. On Monday, a California lawmaker said immigrant officers broke an American citizen’s arm over the weekend. And earlier this month in New York City, an ICE officer shot and wounded a man who DHS argued had a previous grand larceny conviction and a number of prior arrests.

In today’s issue: Trump-Graham rally Senate debates in Michigan, Kansas Ramaswamy takes responsibility for Acton ad LeBron’s 76ers debut Programming note: We’re Joshua Feldstein and Julia Boehning, filling in for Cate…
articles.body:
It’s Wednesday, and Washington is buzzing for the Wizards’ season opener tonight against the Milwaukee Bucks.

Ramaswamy takes responsibility for Acton ad

Programming note : We’re Joshua Feldstein and Julia Boehning, filling in for Cate today. Please send us your tips, comments and story ideas to jfeldstein@thehill.com and jboehning@thehill.com .

President Trump is slated to campaign alongside Sen. Darline Graham (R-S.C.) in South Carolina tonight — a meetup coming just days after he waived sanctions against Russia outlined in a legislative package named after her brother, the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.).

While some Republicans have slammed these waivers — which Trump introduced via executive order late Friday — as a slight on Lindsey Graham’s legacy, the late senator’s sister stopped short of criticizing the president for the move. Though Darline Graham conceded that “personally, I would choose to keep the pressure on Russia.”

“The president and I share the same goal, which is to end the war, get gas and diesel prices down,” she told The Associated Press on Saturday. “The sanctions bill is one of the tools he can use to do that. It’s up to him whether or not he chooses to use it.”

Now the pair are set to meet up in Clemson, S.C., at 7 p.m. EDT — the next stop in the president’s seven-day, seven-stop campaign blitz less than two weeks out from Election Day.

Endorsement power: The president sang Graham’s praises this morning in a Truth Social post, writing, “Darline Graham is GREAT!”

Trump’s endorsement played a crucial role in securing a primary runoff victory for Graham despite scrutiny surrounding her qualifications for the role. South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster (R) appointed Graham, who had never held political office, to the Senate after her brother’s unexpected death in July.

Trump was quick to boost Graham after her appointment and maintained his support throughout the election cycle. The president last campaigned with the senator a week ahead of the state’s primary runoff and shortly after her dodgy performance during a debate, in which she flubbed a question on national security.

The Hill’s nonpartisan election forecasting partner, Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), gives Graham a 70 percent chance of beating Democratic opponent Annie Andrews.

Meanwhile, in Moscow: Kremlin officials said Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. after meeting with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg, the AP first reported this morning.

The meeting came a day after Witkoff met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky , who has grown increasingly critical of Trump in the wake of the Russian sanctions waiver and Ukraine’s outage of Starshield, the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink internet.

The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that tech mogul Elon Musk , a close ally to the president, called for the slowdown.

Former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed will go head-to-head once again tonight in a debate for Michigan’s open Senate seat.

As a reminder, the first debate on Oct. 8 made WOOD TV8 moderator Rick Albin say, “In 30 years of doing debates, I’ve never seen it continue during the commercial. But it did.”

Round 1 went off the rails: The first debate between Rogers and El-Sayed featured mostly personal jabs at each other.

The GOP candidate alleged that El-Sayed and his family have ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist religiopolitical organization founded in Egypt in the 1920s.

Rogers also labeled the Democrat a fake medical professional. El-Sayed received a medical degree from Columbia University and a doctorate in public health from Oxford University.

El-Sayed fought back, labeling Rogers as a “rubber stamp” and “sock puppet” for Trump.

In the first debate, the two zoomed in on the Trump administration’s relationship with Israel, the nationwide immigration crackdown and rising fuel/energy prices connected to the Iran war.

Brotherhood comments bound to come up: El-Sayed was asked a question during a Saturday town hall event in Michigan on whether he would “disavow the Muslim Brotherhood.”

El-Sayed responded, saying, “Sure. Yeah, absolutely,” but, “Why are you asking the question?”

The Democrat continued to bash the question, adding, “Have you asked everybody in your life if they disavow them? So why are you asking me?”

Bridge Michigan reported last month there is no evidence connecting El-Sayed to the organization, but Rogers will most likely pounce on the opportunity to bring it up again in Wednesday’s debate.

articles.title: Amy Acton’s estranged mother drags her in crazy attack ad
articles.summary: Acton’s enemies have run a political ad in which they enlisted Acton’s own mother, whom she has been estranged from since she was 12, to call her a liar. This is a very disturbing ad, for several reasons.
articles.body:
Amy Acton is the Democratic candidate for governor in Ohio, and her opponent is Republican Vivek Ramaswamy. Long-time viewers know I’m personally a fan of Ramaswamy, as he shares many, though not all, of my limited-government libertarian views.

But today I’m speaking in defense of Acton, and against a vicious smear of which she is the victim.

Acton’s enemies have run a political ad in which they enlisted Acton’s own mother, whom she has been estranged from since she was 12, to call her a liar. This is a very disturbing ad, for several reasons.

First, I want to be clear that I think it’s incredibly sickening to bother one’s family members and compel them to speak ill of their relations for partisan political purposes.

And the details here make it even worse. According to Amy Acton , her mother lost custody of her when she was 12 after the mother’s then husband, who was not Amy Acton’s father, sexually abused her. Amy Acton’s brother has spoken up in support of that account, not the mother’s.

I obviously cannot state for certain which account is correct, but there has been additional media reporting and corroboration in support of Amy Acton.

Donna Arthur is clearly motivated to clear her own name — and is willing to throw her daughter under the bus to accomplish it. How shameful is that? To allow yourself to be used by your daughter’s enemies for their political project? Have you not caused her to suffer enough?

Politics is an ugly, ugly business, and attack ads are well in bounds for any campaign. By all means, highlight Amy Acton’s liberal policies and how they are a bad fit for Ohio, a red state. And if you have proof that she has misrepresented her background, then fine. But this isn’t proof at all: this is a personal smear.

I could not reach the Ramaswamy campaign for comment about this, and it’s not immediately clear to me who is responsible for the ad, and whether the Republican candidate signed off on it. If he did, it was a huge, huge mistake. I actually bet Ohioans who see this will become more sympathetic to Acton, not less. It highlights her difficult background and the fact that she has not enjoyed her mother’s support throughout her adult life — and certainly doesn’t now.

Indeed, online betting site Polymarket now put Ramaswamy’s odds of winning the governor’s race at an abysmal 30 percent . In Ohio, a state Donald Trump won three times. Play stupid games, win stupid prizes.

Robby Soave is co-host of The Hill’s commentary show “Rising” and a senior editor for Reason Magazine. This column is an edited transcription of his daily commentary.

articles.title: Jon Stewart torches Trump’s dealings with Russia
articles.summary: Americans could get little relief at the pump while Moscow gets sanctions relief and another opportunity to negotiate directly with Washington on their terms only.
articles.body:
Jon Stewart hilariously pulled out a Russian nesting doll to explain what he sees as the layers of stupidity in President Trump’s latest move involving Russia.

“The Daily Show” host was reacting to the administration’s decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports , even as Russia continues its war against Ukraine .

Stewart responded to Energy Secretary Christopher Wright explaining the rationale on CNN:

Wright: “This is a motivation for Russia to figure out how they can actually export some diesel.”

Stewart: “Why would we motivate a group to sell diesel when we just put sanctions on them for selling diesel? Doing the opposite within a month is insane. It is illogical. It is incoherent!”

Exactly — what exactly is America getting in return?

The White House is under pressure to bring down fuel costs ahead of this midterm elections, with diesel prices now at record highs. But financial institutions like Goldman Sachs note that the Russia sanctions waiver might trim at most a penny or two per gallon , leaving consumers with no meaningful relief at gas stations.

So Americans could get little relief at the pump while Moscow gets sanctions relief and another opportunity to negotiate directly with Washington on their terms only.

Meanwhile, the relationship between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is deteriorating over intelligence sharing, sanctions, attacks on Russian energy infrastructure and the actual terms of a potential peace deal.

On Monday, Trump questioned Zelensky’s understanding of the situation and suggested it was “time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine.”

Zelensky has said he is open to negotiations, provided Ukraine’s security can be guaranteed, but that Ukraine cannot be expected to accept a peace deal negotiated over its head. And reports that Russia is exploring a summit involving Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping raise some serious concerns about who gets to determine Ukraine’s future. No European leaders have been invited to this meeting.

Russian President Vladimir Putin may understand something Trump keeps overlooking: He doesn’t have to win every battle if he can persuade the American president to weaken the pressure on Russia and give Moscow a seat at the head of the table.

Putin gets to pursue his military objectives while Trump gets to claim he’s working toward peace and claim he’s lower fuel prices. But if the economic benefits are marginal and Ukraine is pressured into concessions, all that’s happening is the U.S. is getting played for a fool and Ukraine is getting left out to dry.

Diplomacy is necessary, but not without credible security guarantees — otherwise Ukraine and our other European allies will just be vulnerable to the next invasion when Russia feels like it.

Lindsey Granger is a NewsNation contributor and co-host of The Hill’s commentary show “Rising.” This column is an edited transcription of her on-air commentary.

articles.title: Vance ‘disgusted’ by Republicans decrying Ramaswamy ad with Acton’s mother
articles.summary: Vice President Vance criticized the response by some Republicans to a campaign ad for Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy (R), saying he is “disgusted” by those in his party who pushed back on the video. “I have to admit that I’m a little bit disgusted when I see Republicans across the country who are whining…
articles.body:
Vice President Vance criticized the response by some Republicans to a campaign ad for Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy (R), saying he is “disgusted” by those in his party who pushed back on the video.

“I have to admit that I’m a little bit disgusted when I see Republicans across the country who are whining more about that advertisement than they are about what the congressional Democrats and other Democrats want to do to the United States of America,” Vance said at a fraud task force press conference Wednesday.

The ad features the mother of Ramaswamy’s Democratic opponent, Amy Acton, who accuses Acton of being a “liar” and saying “my daughter needs help.”

Acton’s brother released a statement and a competing video hours later saying that he and Acton have been estranged from their mother for years because she stayed married to the man who sexually abused Acton at a young age. Acton was removed from her mother’s care at the age of 12, something unmentioned in the Ramaswamy ad.

Acton is in a competitive race for Ohio governor, but her lead has expanded in recent polls. Decision Desk HQ, a partner of The Hill, gives Acton a 60 percent chance of defeating Ramaswamy.

Vance, a former Ohio senator, again defended Ramaswamy while rallying with him in the Buckeye State Wednesday.

“Vivek Ramaswamy had the audacity to run a TV commercial which calls it out like it is and calls Amy Acton a liar,” Vance said. “Whatever you think about any of the TV advertisements, focus on the substance and focus on the facts.”

The personal nature and controversy surrounding the ad led Democrats and some Republicans to condemn it and call on Ramaswamy, who admitted Tuesday that the ad was from his campaign, to change course.

Axios reported Tuesday that Ramaswamy’s campaign will now spend $4 million on airing the ad statewide.

Vance said at the press conference that he is not concerned about the ad and is only focused on Republicans winning Ohio.

“Whether the ad was appropriate or not is not really my concern,” Vance said. “What is my concern is who is going to govern the next generation of American government, who is going to win the Senate race in the state of Ohio, who is going to win the governor’s race in the state of Ohio?”

“Politics is a tough business,” Vance added. “My message to my fellow elected Republicans is if you actually believe in the things you say you believe in, stop whining about an advertisement and go win the race in 13 days.”

articles.title: Cooper holds 13-point lead over Whatley in NC Senate race: Poll
articles.summary: A new poll found former North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper (D) holds a 13-point lead over his GOP opponent Michael Whatley in the state’s Senate race less than two weeks away from Election Day. The Elon University poll reported 52 percent of respondents favored Cooper, 39 percent backed Whatley, 6 percent were undecided and 3…
articles.body:
A new poll found former North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper (D) holds a 13-point lead over his GOP opponent Michael Whatley in the state’s Senate race less than two weeks away from Election Day.

The Elon University poll reported 52 percent of respondents favored Cooper, 39 percent backed Whatley, 6 percent were undecided and 3 percent chose Libertarian candidate Shannon Bray, Green Party candidate Michael Dublin or “someone else.”

In a forced-choice question, where undecided voters were asked to make a choice in the Senate race, 54 percent chose Cooper and 43 percent picked Whatley.

Cooper and Whatley are looking to take the Senate seat currently occupied by Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), who announced he would not be running for reelection. It is one seat Democrats are hoping to pick up in their effort to regain control of the upper chamber.

Cooper led among independent respondents with 50 percent choosing him, 24 percent picking Whatley and 17 percent still undecided.

Whatley held leads among white voters, though Cooper led among Black, Hispanic and female voters. Both candidates were tied among male respondents at 42 percent.

“Cooper’s lead among registered voters overall is smaller than his lead among the subset of registered voters who say they are likely to vote, implying opportunity for Republicans if they can motivate more of their base to turn out,” noted Jason Husser, director of the Elon University Poll and professor of political science and public policy.

In an effort to invigorate GOP voters , President Trump made a stop in Greenville, N.C. , after Vice President Vance visited Hendersonville, N.C .

Husser said results of the poll indicated that, among Republicans in the Tar Heel State, a candidate’s endorsement from Trump did not make them less likely to support the endorsed candidate, and even the president’s $5,000 dividend proposal did not appear to sway North Carolina voters toward Republicans. Trump previously stated dividend checks would be doled out only if the GOP maintains its majorities in the House and Senate after the midterm elections.

Thirty percent of those polled said Trump’s dividend promise makes them less likely to vote for the GOP while 16 percent said it makes them more likely to, and 50 percent said the president’s promise makes no difference in their vote.

“Even among those who approve of the President’s job performance, most said the dividend makes no difference to their voting decision. However, the President’s endorsement still resonates with his base,” Husser added.

Of the registered voters surveyed, 43 percent said a Trump endorsement would “make it less likely they would vote for a candidate,” compared to 25 percent who said it would make them more likely to vote for a candidate and 26 percent who said a Trump endorsement made no difference.

The Elon University poll was conducted between Sept. 29-Oct. 8 among 800 North Carolina adults. The margin of error was 4.03 percentage points.

articles.title: Social Security corrects death, citizenship information for millions of numbers
articles.summary: The Social Security Administration (SSA) announced Tuesday it corrected millions of Social Security number (SSN) database files, including death records and citizenship information, partially using the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) service. “The Social Security Number database is our country’s books and records. The database’s accuracy is essential to maintaining integrity of government services…
articles.body:
The Social Security Administration (SSA) announced Tuesday it corrected millions of Social Security number (SSN) database files, including death records and citizenship information, partially using the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) service.

“The Social Security Number database is our country’s books and records. The database’s accuracy is essential to maintaining integrity of government services for citizens,” Frank Bisignano, the agency’s commissioner, said in a press release . “Accurate SSN records prevent fraud across federal programs and support the proper administration of benefits.”

Among these corrections, the agency said it updated about 25 million records with missing citizenship information with the help of SAVE, a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) service used to determine eligibility for certain federal programs.

SAVE came into the national spotlight when President Trump directed the DHS to ensure election officials had appropriate resources to verify their voters’ citizenship, leading to a significant overhaul of the system. Trump previously mandated states turn over their voter rolls to the department in order to identify and strike non-U.S. citizens from their respective lists using the federal technology — an order a federal judge blocked in early October.

But the judge’s ruling did not strike the service itself, and the administration is continuing its antifraud push ahead of November’s midterms.

“SSA is currently in the process of correcting an additional 8.5 million records with inaccurate citizenship status,” the release states.

According to the SSA, it has corrected nearly 15 percent of all active SSNs since the beginning of the Trump administration.

As a part of its effort, the agency said it added 17 million dates of death to records that it claims previously lacked such information. The agency said it did so by using a combination of internal SSA systems and State Department data.

“The first time SSA has undertaken a record‑integrity initiative of this magnitude and marks a significant step toward strengthening the SSN system for the American public,” Bisignano said.

articles.title: Federal grand jury indicts man shot by ICE officer in Austin
articles.summary: A Venezuelan man who was shot and wounded by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer during a traffic stop in Austin last month has been indicted on a federal assault charge. A federal grand jury indicted Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, on one count of assaulting, resisting, impeding and obstructing a federal officer. Prosecutors…
articles.body:
A Venezuelan man who was shot and wounded by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer during a traffic stop in Austin last month has been indicted on a federal assault charge.

A federal grand jury indicted Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, on one count of assaulting, resisting, impeding and obstructing a federal officer. Prosecutors allege he used his vehicle as a deadly weapon while attempting to flee ICE officers during a traffic stop in September.

The indictment follows a criminal complaint filed by the Department of Homeland Security, which accused Garces Perez of striking an ICE officer with his car before leading officers on a brief high-speed chase through a residential area.

An ICE officer subsequently shot Garces Perez, leaving him hospitalized with a gunshot wound. He was later taken into custody at an immigration detention facility, with the bullet still lodged in his spine.

He faces up to 20 years in federal prison if convicted, according to the Justice Department.

According to a federal affidavit, agents approached Garces Perez after identifying him as someone with a final order of removal. He initially complied with their request for identification but refused to exit his vehicle.

Garces Perez later told investigators that he wanted to move his car so his wife could pick it up after his arrest. He admitted to fleeing the scene, and prosecutors say his driver’s side mirror struck an officer in the torso.

Another ICE officer, who was not wearing a body camera during the incident, claimed Garces Perez attempted to strike him with the vehicle. The officer fired into the car’s rear window, hitting Garces Perez in the back.

The shooting drew scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers and local officials, who questioned the circumstances surrounding the encounter and called for an independent investigation.

Austin Mayor Kirk Watson (D) pushed for local authorities to have a role in investigating the incident.

“As mayor of the city of Austin, I’m very angry about this,” Watson said at a Sept. 20 news conference. “A person being shot in the streets of Austin by someone reporting to be law enforcement, particularly when it’s ICE, is something that causes me to be unhappy and angry.”

articles.title: Carville says he has ‘Trump derangement syndrome’: ‘I can’t sleep’

Carville said in an appearance on podcast network Politicon’s YouTube channel that political commentators like comedian Bill…
articles.body:
Democratic strategist James Carville quipped Tuesday he “can’t sleep” because of his “Trump derangement syndrome,” referring to the fake condition some use to describe a person with an intense worry about and fixation on what President Trump does.

Carville said in an appearance on podcast network Politicon’s YouTube channel that political commentators like comedian Bill Maher have accused him of having the fake syndrome, which the president sometimes refers to as TDS . But the strategist went on to embrace the label.

“I got it, and I want it, and I want it to get worse,” Carville said. “If I could take a pill that would help me hate that motherf‑‑‑er more and obsess on him more, I would take that pill. Maybe we can have a pharmacological intervention, I don’t know.”

Carville said earlier in the clip that he hates “the son of a b‑‑‑‑, I hate what he’s doing to this country. I’m obsessed with it. I can’t sleep at night.”

The lead campaign strategist to former President Clinton called the “condition” a “horrific , consuming disease,” adding that “millions” of Americans are afflicted by viewing Trump as a “criminal of the first order.”

“In other words, we think this administration is so corrupt that when somebody tallies it up, hopefully it’ll be some genius at The Atlantic at some time in the future, will conclude that more was stolen from Jan. 20, 2025, and Oct. 21, 2026, than the entire history of the country,” he continued, comparing Trump’s controversies to others throughout U.S. history, such as the Teapot Dome Scandal of the 1920s.

He added that critics with TDS “can’t think of anything else” and that it is an “obsession, and if you don’t understand that, you don’t understand the country that you’re reporting on.”

He closed the video saying that while he has TDS, he hoped to “get rid of it sometime around, oh, I don’t know, 22:00 hours, 3 November 2026” — the date of the upcoming midterm elections.

The president frequently uses the pejorative moniker on his opponents. He notably claimed filmmaker Rob Reiner — a known Trump critic — and his wife were killed in December “due to the anger he caused others through his massive, unyielding, and incurable affliction with a mind crippling disease known as TRUMP DERANGEMENT SYNDROME.”

The term has been linked to a similar label conservative columnist Charles Krauthammer coined, “Bush derangement syndrome,” which referred to an obsession and anger with former President George W. Bush during his presidency.

Carville, long nicknamed the “Ragin’ Cajun,” is a vocal critic of Trump. The strategist often says he believes the president’s unpopularity could drive him out of office and cause him to lose support .

In June, he predicted Trump would be so “miserable” following the midterms and “bored” by the Iran war that he would leave the presidency by “Easter 2027.”

articles.body:
GOP Sen. Bernie Moreno (Ohio) said Tuesday he will introduce legislation to expand access to the Trump administration’s investment accounts for children to Americans younger than 40.

“This is a game-changer and I’ll lead the bill in the Senate to make it happen,” Moreno wrote on the social platform X . “Trump Accounts are already transforming lives for families across America.”

The Ohio Republican argued that raising the age limit for Trump Accounts will “give hardworking Americans powerful new tools to buy homes, wipe out student debt, and invest in their own futures.”

Senators are on recess and are scheduled to return on Nov. 9. Republicans hold a 53-47 edge in the Senate and are attempting to maintain control of the upper chamber in the November midterms .

Altimeter CEO Brad Gerstner, a proponent of the accounts , recently told the New York Post he is working to expand their scope to anyone younger than 40.

Gerstner added the legislation would propose making funding for the accounts permanent — the Treasury Department is depositing $1,000 into the account of any American child born from the start of 2025 through 2028.

The Hill has reached out to the White House and Treasury Department for comment. The administration created the accounts under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which President Trump signed into law in July 2025.

The president said Tuesday his administration is looking into “an alternative” version of Trump Accounts for adults.

“We are looking at something different, because it is somewhat of a different thing, having to do with adults,” Trump told reporters.

More than 70 million children have an account, according to Invest America , after the Treasury Department automatically enrolled more than 60 million children in the program.

The federal government will invest the accounts in the State Street SPDR Portfolio exchange-traded fund (ETF), which tracks the S&P 500. Parents will also be able to choose between four other ETFs to invest their child’s account in.

Dozens of companies are matching the Treasury Department’s $1,000 contribution to babies born from 2025 to 2028.

Dell CEO Michael Dell and his wife, Susan Dell, have sent $250 to the accounts of 25 million children living in zip codes with a median family income of $117,300 or less — a donation totaling $6.25 billion.

Tech mogul Elon Musk also said Monday he will give one share of his SpaceX company to every child in the U.S. next year. The president later confirmed Musk will make his contribution to children’s Trump Accounts.
